newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian beet harvest still delayed by rain.
newsitem.headline: Croatian beet harvest still delayed by rain.

text.p: Croatian beet growers are waiting for a longer break in the rain to continue the much delayed harvest which has yielded betweeen 140,000 and 150,000 tonnes of beet so far this year, the agriculture ministry said on Wednesday.
"If it remains dry so that machinery can go out, perhaps the harvest can restart in two or three days and then it might be completed by next week," official Irena Ljesevic told Reuters.
She said only 15 percent of 21,738 hectares planted to beet had been harvested so far, with growers reporting yields around 43 tonnes per hectare.
Andrija Kristek of the Sugar Beet Institute in Osijek said laboratory tests showed yields were boosted above the average for the past few years by the rains and could reach 45 tonnes.

Sugar content has also improved since the second beet test, and now varies between 10 and 17 percent, Kristek said. It was in a 11.5-15.5 percent range in the first half of September. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
